```{r setup, include=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

The best linear unbiased predictor of the random effects is
$\tilde b = G Z^\top V^{-1}(y - X\hat\beta)$.
For a random intercept, subject $i$ gets
$\tilde b_{0i} = k_i\,(\bar y_{i\cdot} - \bar x_{i\cdot}^\top\hat\beta)$ with shrinkage factor
$k_i = n_i\sigma_b^2/(n_i\sigma_b^2 + \sigma^2)$.

```{r data}
library(lme4)
data(sleepstudy)
m_ri <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject), data = sleepstudy)
vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(m_ri))$vcov
sigma_b2 <- vc[1]; sigma2 <- vc[2]
beta <- fixef(m_ri)
```

## BLUP with the matrix formula

```{r matrix-blup}
y <- sleepstudy$Reaction
X <- model.matrix(~ Days, sleepstudy)
Z <- model.matrix(~ 0 + Subject, sleepstudy)
G <- sigma_b2 * diag(ncol(Z))
V <- Z %*% G %*% t(Z) + sigma2 * diag(nrow(Z))
b_tilde <- G %*% t(Z) %*% solve(V, y - X %*% beta)
head(cbind(by_hand = b_tilde[, 1], ranef = ranef(m_ri)$Subject[, 1]))
```

## BLUP as a shrunken raw deviation

```{r shrinkage}
n_i  <- 10
k    <- n_i * sigma_b2 / (n_i * sigma_b2 + sigma2)
k
raw  <- tapply(y - X %*% beta, sleepstudy$Subject, mean)   # ybar_i - xbar_i' beta_hat
blup <- ranef(m_ri)$Subject[, 1]
head(cbind(raw = raw, k_times_raw = k * raw, blup = blup))
```

Subject 309 has a raw deviation of $-83.3$ ms and a BLUP of $-77.8$ ms:
it keeps 93.5% of its own evidence.

## Unbalanced data: fewer observations, more shrinkage

Keep only Days 0--1 (two observations) for the first six subjects and all
ten days for the others.

```{r unbalanced}
few <- levels(sleepstudy$Subject)[1:6]
sl_unb <- subset(sleepstudy, !(Subject %in% few) | Days <= 1)
table(table(droplevels(sl_unb$Subject)))
m_unb <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject), data = sl_unb)
vcu <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(m_unb))$vcov
ni_u  <- as.vector(table(sl_unb$Subject))
k_u   <- ni_u * vcu[1] / (ni_u * vcu[1] + vcu[2])
raw_u <- tapply(sl_unb$Reaction - model.matrix(~ Days, sl_unb) %*% fixef(m_unb),
                sl_unb$Subject, mean)
blup_u <- ranef(m_unb)$Subject[, 1]
res <- data.frame(n_i = ni_u, k_i = round(k_u, 3), raw = round(raw_u, 1),
                  blup = round(blup_u, 1), ratio = round(blup_u / raw_u, 3))  # ratio = k_i
res[c(1:3, 7:9), ]
```

## The same idea for random slopes

With `(Days | Subject)`, `coef()` returns $\hat\beta + \tilde b_i$ for each subject;
compare with the separate `lm` fits.

```{r slopes}
m_ris <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject), data = sleepstudy)
np <- coef(lmList(Reaction ~ Days | Subject, data = sleepstudy))
pp <- coef(m_ris)$Subject
c(sd_slopes_no_pooling = sd(np[, 2]), sd_slopes_lmm = sd(pp[, 2]),
  sigma_b1_hat = attr(VarCorr(m_ris)$Subject, "stddev")[2])
```

The BLUP slopes vary less than the separate slopes (shrinkage), and even less
than $\hat\sigma_{b1}$: predicted random effects are not a sample from $N(0, G)$.
